how_it_works: After the 'Experience' heading, a full-viewport section is pinned (GSAP ScrollTrigger `pin: true`, `start: 'top top'`) and the user's VERTICAL scroll is translated into HORIZONTAL motion of an inner track ('fake' horizontal scroll). A wrapper holding N role 'chapters' laid side-by-side is animated `x`/`xPercent` to the left as vertical scroll progresses: `gsap.to(track, { x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth), ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, pin: true, scrub: 1, end: '+=' + track.scrollWidth } })`. The scroll budget is set by `end` (roughly the total horizontal travel), so 5 beats each ~1 viewport wide = ~4x viewport of vertical scroll consumed while the section stays fixed. Each chapter is one role (nference FT -> nference intern -> AMC clinical -> DEXTER ML -> Animations Media) presented as a card/panel that slides in from the right. Because the horizontal movement is NOT a native scroll, any per-chapter reveals (title split, bullet stagger, proof chip) must be tied to the master tween via `containerAnimation: horizontalTween` rather than a normal ScrollTrigger. What MOVES: the horizontal track and the panels riding it (x translate). What STAYS: the pinned frame, a persistent 'Experience' label, and a horizontal progress bar / '02 / 05' counter so users always know how far the filmstrip runs and can escape. The critical constraints: `ease: 'none'` on the track tween (otherwise scroll and content desync — the #1 mistake), `scrub` for jitter-forgiveness (Lenis smoothing helps on trackpads), and a mobile breakpoint that abandons the whole pinned-horizontal mechanism.
visual_structure: A single beat is a full-height panel (roughly one viewport wide) in a horizontally-laid-out flex track: small monospace date range top-left (e.g. '2024 — present'), an oversized Fraunces role title (e.g. 'ML Engineer'), an Inter org + location line, 2-3 short Inter bullets (<= 2 lines each), and one maroon proof chip (metric/stack, e.g. 'clinical NLP · 40% faster review'). Panels sit edge-to-edge like frames of a filmstrip; an optional faint oversized ghost year or a thin maroon hairline 'timeline rail' runs across the top spanning all frames to signal chronology (left = earliest, right = latest). As the track scrubs left, the current panel exits stage-left while the next enters stage-right; per-panel micro-motion (title line-reveal, bullet stagger, chip fade) fires as each frame reaches viewport center. A persistent HORIZONTAL progress bar (maroon fill on paper) or '02 / 05' counter is docked to the pinned frame so the sideways distance is legible. Legibility law: at any scroll position exactly one panel's title + org should be centered and fully readable — avoid two half-panels competing for attention at rest (scroll-snap or generous panel width helps).
motion_recipe: GSAP: build ONE horizontal master tween with `ease: 'none'` (mandatory — non-linear ease desyncs scroll from position) moving `xPercent`/`x` of the track; attach `ScrollTrigger` with `pin: true`, `scrub: 0.8-1`, `end` computed from track width, `invalidateOnRefresh: true`, `anticipatePin: 1`. Drive all in-panel reveals with `containerAnimation: masterTween` (pin and snap are NOT available on containerAnimation triggers — use scroll-snap CSS or `snap` on the master tween instead if you want frame-locking). Animate ONLY `transform`/`opacity` (compositor thread, `force3D: true`); never `left`/`width`. Stagger bullets ~0.08-0.12s within a beat; title via SplitText line/clip reveal. Prevent FOUC with CSS `opacity:0` + `gsap.fromTo`. Init inside `document.fonts.ready.then(() => { init(); ScrollTrigger.refresh(); })` since Fraunces/Inter swap shifts measured widths. Gate the entire pin+horizontal mechanism behind `gsap.matchMedia()` at `(min-width: 768px)` AND `(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Set `ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true })`; optionally pair with Lenis for smooth trackpad scrubbing. What NOT to animate: the pinned trigger element itself (animate the inner track/children — animating the trigger breaks pin-spacer math); layout props; no aggressive zoom/flash; do NOT hijack scroll on mobile.
reduced_motion: Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (and outside the `no-preference` matchMedia branch), drop the pin and the horizontal scrub entirely and re-flow the same filmstrip panels into a normal VERTICAL stack in document flow — each role a static card with date, role, org, bullets, proof chip, all visible, zero scroll-linked motion. Substitute chronology cues, don't delete them: keep a static maroon spine or numbered '01–05' markers so left-to-right order becomes top-to-bottom order. This vertical stack is ALSO the mandatory mobile fallback (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow: no 2-D scrolling of text at 320px / 400% zoom) and is what a fast-scanning recruiter actually prefers — so the a11y path, the mobile path, and the scannable path are the same single-column layout.
brand_fit: MEDIUM (LOW if it becomes the only way to read Experience). Reason: A pinned horizontal filmstrip is high desktop 'wow' and echoes the cinematic hero energy, and an editorial maroon-on-paper Fraunces filmstrip can look genuinely premium rather than purple-SaaS slop. BUT it collides hard with this audience: recruiters scan in ~3-10s in an F-pattern, and horizontal/sideways-scroll is repeatedly flagged (Adrian Roselli, NN/g Katie Sherwin 'Beware Horizontal Scrolling', Bogdan Cerovac) as high-friction — users don't expect to scroll sideways, keyboard users can't reach/operate the region without `tabindex=0` + arrow handling, voice-control and screen-magnifier users struggle to find and drive the scroller, and scroll-snap can strand content. Pinning + fake-horizontal is the most fragile pattern on mobile (pin-spacer height doubling, iOS/Android URL-bar resize) — and 68% of recruiter traffic is mobile, where it MUST fall back to vertical anyway. Verdict: acceptable only as a desktop 'signature' layer over a genuinely vertical, keyboard-operable, reduced-motion-safe base — never as the sole reading mode. If the horizontal version disappeared, a recruiter should lose zero information.
steal: Steal the FILMSTRIP FRAMING, not the sideways scroll-jack: reuse the panel layout (date / big Fraunces title / org / short bullets / maroon proof chip) and the thin maroon chronology rail with a '02 / 05' progress counter, but consider realizing 'chapters' as a horizontally-arranged, keyboard-focusable native-overflow scroller (`overflow-x:auto`, `tabindex=0`, role+label, scroll-snap, visible edge-shadow affordance) with prev/next buttons — you keep the left-to-right career-timeline metaphor and the editorial frames while letting the browser own scrolling (arrow keys, swipe, scrollbar) instead of hijacking vertical scroll. That delivers most of the 'filmstrip' delight with far less a11y and mobile risk than a pinned scrub.
avoid: Avoid converting vertical scroll into forced horizontal travel through all 5 roles (classic scroll-jack): it defies user expectation, traps time-boxed recruiters, and is a documented a11y minefield — keyboard users can't operate it without explicit `tabindex=0`+arrow support, magnifier/voice-control users can't find the scroller, in-page find and anchor focus can strand off-screen (risking WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured), and at 400% zoom it fails 1.4.10 Reflow. Concretely: don't disable native vertical scroll, don't hide roles behind sideways scrub with no progress indicator/exit, don't rely on `ease` other than `'none'` (desync), don't nest a horizontal scroller inside another scroll region, and NEVER ship the pinned-horizontal version on mobile — always reflow to a single vertical column.
live_examples: Codrops 'Building a Scrollable and Draggable Timeline with GSAP' (tympanus.net/codrops/2022/01/03/building-a-scrollable-and-draggable-timeline-with-gsap/) — a horizontal date timeline synced to scroll + drag + click, the closest documented analog to a filmstrip of chronological 'chapters'
